title: Derived direct-image comparisons commute with open restriction and reassociation
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of positive characteristic different from $\ell$, a fixed algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and a finite intermediate extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. All schemes below are separated and finite type over $k$, and all morphisms are $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\Lambda=E$ or $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ with the pulled-back condensed coefficient rings $\Lambda_T$ and the finite-subextension convention of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring; sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed; sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use the ordinary unbounded categories $D_T=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T})$ and their total right derived module direct images [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories; sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. Write $\kappa_{g,f}:R(gf)_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rg_*Rf_*$ for the resolution-normalized comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. Then:

1. For $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ\xrightarrow hT$, the two maps from $R(hgf)_*$ to $Rh_*Rg_*Rf_*$ agree:
$$ (Rh_*\kappa_{g,f})\circ\kappa_{h,gf}=(\kappa_{h,g}Rf_*)\circ\kappa_{hg,f}. $$
2. For $f:S\to T$ and a quasi-compact open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow T$, put $S_U=S\times_TU$, with open $j_S:S_U\hookrightarrow S$ and restricted map $f_U:S_U\to U$. There is a natural isomorphism
$$\rho_{f,j}:j^*Rf_*\xrightarrow{\sim}R(f_U)_*j_S^*.$$
For a K-injective representative $I$ of an object of $D_S$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex], this is the class of the canonical underived restriction isomorphism $j^*f_*I\cong(f_U)_*j_S^*I$, whose value on a site object $V\to U$ is the identity on $I(V\times_T S)$. Module structures are transported along the inverse coefficient-ring comparisons of [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients].
3. These restriction isomorphisms commute with successive open restrictions. They also commute with composition: for $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gT$ and $j:U\hookrightarrow T$, let $j_Y:Y_U\hookrightarrow Y$, $j_X:X_U\hookrightarrow X$ be the pulled-back opens. The two maps from $j^*R(gf)_*$ to $R(g_U)_*R(f_U)_*j_X^*$ agree:
$$ (R(g_U)_*\rho_{f,j_Y})\circ(\rho_{g,j}Rf_*)\circ(j^*\kappa_{g,f})=(\kappa_{g_U,f_U}j_X^*)\circ\rho_{gf,j}. $$
All formulas insert the canonical functor associators and fibre-product identifications; for identity maps and identity open immersions the comparisons are identities.

source.place: The composition isomorphism, equality Rq_*Rr_* = R(qr)_*; Canonicity and associativity, restriction normalization of all comparison maps. Extracted from returned Step 2.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-kinjective-direct-image-open-word-model] to the pulled-back coefficient system. Its coefficient-map hypothesis holds by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], for both $E$ and the specified finite-subextension $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Thus every direct image and open restriction in the formulas is computed on one initial K-injective $I$. In [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition], choose the identity resolution of $f_*I$. Its normalization identifies the specified $\kappa_{g,f}$ with the class of $c_{g,f,I}$ from [lem-sfb-module-direct-image-open-pasting]; this identifies the given comparison, rather than choosing one.

source.place: Composition isomorphism and Canonicity and associativity; assembly of the two extracted arguments

proof.text: For an open square use $\beta_{f,j}$ of [lem-sfb-module-direct-image-open-pasting]. Its component is the identity on $I(V\times_T S)$ after the stated fibre-product identification, and its module actions use the inverse coefficient comparisons. By [lem-sfb-kinjective-direct-image-open-word-model](iii), its degreewise maps descend to a natural isomorphism $\rho_{f,j}:j^*Rf_*\cong R(f_U)_*j_S^*$ with precisely that K-injective formula. The transition formula there supplies independence of $I$ and naturality for every derived arrow. This proves clause 2.

source.place: Composition isomorphism and Canonicity and associativity; assembly of the two extracted arguments

proof.text: Equation (b) of [lem-sfb-module-direct-image-open-pasting] is an equality of transformations between underived words. Apply the diagram-descent assertion of [lem-sfb-kinjective-direct-image-open-word-model] and substitute the identification of $\kappa$ from step 1. It becomes exactly clause 1, with its canonical associators. Equation (c) descends in the same way, using step 2, and gives successive-open compatibility.

source.place: Composition isomorphism and Canonicity and associativity; assembly of the two extracted arguments

proof.text: Finally apply the same diagram-descent assertion of [lem-sfb-kinjective-direct-image-open-word-model] to equation (d) of [lem-sfb-module-direct-image-open-pasting]. Each whiskering is computed on a K-injective image of $I$, so its factors are exactly the $\kappa$ of step 1 and $\rho$ of step 2. Its source is $j^*R(gf)_*$ and its target is $R(g_U)_*R(f_U)_*j_X^*$, giving the displayed equation of clause 3. The identity constraints of the underived node descend to the asserted identities as well.
